Host pinning correct: EMM Sec 1.2.1 adopts d3(std)=0, differing from Gompf by 1/2, so Gompf d3=-1/2 = EMM xi_0 (verified in full HTML text). Eliashberg uniqueness means any diagram with that d3 is xi_0. Thm 1.14(1) verbatim (fetched full text): in xi_0 knots are L_pm^{i,k+1/2} with tb=i, rot=∓(i-2n+1), tor=k+1/2 if i>2n-1 else k+1. For n=2 (T(2,5)): tb=9 forces i=9>3, rot=∓6, tor>=1/2, doubly excluding (9,2,0). Thm 1.14(3) confirms (9,2,0) occurs uniquely as L_{2,-}^9 in xi_1 (Gompf +1/2): rot=∓(i-7), at i=9 gives 2 for minus sign; other vertices give rot ±4 or different tb. Arithmetic replayed: inputs/artifacts/verify_disproof.py -> VERIFY_DISPROOF_OK 8/8 (re-ran, EXIT 0). No bypass/LOSS reasoning needed: vacuous/moot if objects absent. Limitation honestly stated: depends on correctness of 123pp EMM classification v2; auditor verified statements, not full 123pp proof. No boundary error: tor definition matches EMM convex torsion; tb+rot parity (11 odd) does not already exclude, so EMM use is necessary and sufficient.

Object (T(2,5)) was motivated, but value (absence) is obtained by plugging n=2/i=9 into EMM formulas with no new construction, isotopy movie, Floer computation, or general criterion. Fails the 'not known or mechanically implied' test for narrow exact invariants: any future researcher with EMM derives it in one line. As TARGET audit, it also does not establish the admitted positive collapse; it reports the target vertex was mis-hosted (belongs to Gompf +1/2), which is erratum-level bookkeeping, not a substantive result.
